subject: POC scope adapt: add batch inference API + revised success gates
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@deepretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC scope adapt: add batch inference API + revised success gates

Hi Elena — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned on scope for the POC/trial: 

Summary of ask
- DeepRetail would like us to add a batch inference API for nightly embedding/batch scoring in addition to the interactive chat/intent paths we discussed. The goal is to evaluate cost and throughput for a hybrid workflow (real-time + nightly batch).

Proposed adjustments to the POC (Redwood suggestion)
1) New use case: Batch inference pipeline (ingest CSV -> batch embeddings -> similarity scoring). Redwood provides batch endpoint + integration checklist.
2) Revised success gates: 
   - Throughput: sustain 5000 records/hour on a single dedicated pool (95th percentile).
   - Cost: per-embedding unit cost not to exceed $0.002 on batch runs (operational target).
   - Accuracy: end-to-end retrieval precision @K=10 >= 78% on your eval sample.
   - Latency: interactive chat path unchanged (95th percentile < 300ms for 1-2 turn convs).
3) Timeline: 
   - Week 0 (this week): confirmation of scope and owners.
   - Week 1: Redwood provides integration checklist & sandbox creds. DeepRetail sends representative batch sample (<= 10k rows).
   - Week 2: Ingest + run initial batch; baseline metrics collected.
   - Week 3: Iteration on batching params + final acceptance run.

Owners (proposed)
- DeepRetail: data extract and sample delivery (Elena / Eng).
- Redwood integration: Ben Carter (integration lead) — infra + endpoints.
- Redwood onboarding: Monica Patel — data ingestion support and runbook.
- Redwood evals & metrics: Karthik Iyer — success gate definitions and scoring script.

Attachments: proposed_eval_matrix.xlsx (draft acceptance matrix) and integration_checklist.md.

Please confirm if the timeline and gates look reasonable from your side, and whether you can deliver a 5–10k sample by Tuesday. If so, Ben and Monica will schedule the sandbox handoff and I’ll update the HubSpot deal.

Best,
Hannah

From: Elena Torres <elena@deepretail.com>

Cc: DeepRetail Eng <eng+infra@deepretail.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC scope adapt: add batch inference API + revised success gates

Thanks Hannah — this matches our internal notes and the team is on board to add batch scoring. A few clarifications before we lock timelines: 

1) Sample delivery: we can provide a 8k-row CSV by Tue EOD (central). It will contain IDs, text fields, and a small ground-truth set for a subset (~800 rows).
2) Throughput target: 5k/hr is fine but can you confirm what hardware profile Redwood will run the batch on (V100 vs A100 equiv)? We need to compare with our internal benchmarks.
3) Cost target: the $0.002 per embedding is acceptable as a goal; we’ll flag if our internal baselines differ.

If answers on the infra profile look good we’ll proceed with Tue delivery. Can Ben loop in the sandbox creds and endpoint spec?

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Data Platform | DeepRetail
elena@deepretail.com

Elena — thanks for the quick confirmation and the sample ETA. Two quick answers to your questions and an updated plan: 

- Hardware profile: we will use an A10G-equivalent dedicated node for the baseline batch run. I’ve asked infra to include an A100 run if you want a higher-throughput comparison; we can schedule that as a follow-up.
- Cost calc: Karthik updated the eval matrix to show per-embedding cost based on commodity and reserved capacity; see attached revised spreadsheet.

Next steps (finalized):
- Tue (today): DeepRetail delivers 8k CSV by EOD (Elena).
- Wed: Ben provisions sandbox keys + shares endpoint spec and curl examples.
- Thu: Monica runs onboarding session with Eng and does a live ingest together.
- Fri: First full batch run; Karthik collects metrics and publishes the run report to the shared Drive.

I’ve updated HubSpot (link below) and attached the revised eval matrix. If that schedule works, I’ll create the onboarding calendar invite and include the runbook link.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.
